title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Østerbro: Find the Fast Way
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race two search frontiers—one from the start and one from the goal—across Copenhagen’s street graph. The visualization shows how meeting in the middle slashes exploration while preserving the shortest path guarantee.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Copenhagen’s Østerbro streets turned into a weighted graph for **Bidirectional Dijkstra**! 🌍🗺️

In this visualization, we run Dijkstra *from both ends*: one priority queue expands from the start, the other from the goal. ✅ Once the two frontiers meet (or cross a best-known bound), we stitch the route—often exploring far fewer nodes than classic single-source Dijkstra, while still guaranteeing the **optimal shortest path** on non-negative edge weights.

Graph theory moment: think of intersections as vertices and street segments as weighted edges (distance/time). On real map data, this “meet-in-the-middle” strategy reduces redundant work by shrinking the search radius—like cutting through the neighborhood before the full map is scanned. 📍⚡
